waiting.incident_summary: elbow_flex stalled at 2.9 N·m on the move home; the healer's two checked retries failed
waiting.verdict: Elbow blocked or servo failing: needs hands

hypotheses.claim: Something is jamming the elbow: the stall held in both directions, including the move home.
hypotheses.check: Power off, then move the elbow by hand through its full range. It should turn freely, with no grinding or hard stop.

hypotheses.claim: The elbow servo's gears or motor were damaged by the stall (a C018 heats up fast at 2.9 N·m).
hypotheses.check: After clearing the jam, power on and jog elbow_flex ±20°. If it still stalls or reads over 60 °C, swap in the spare.

hypotheses.claim: A loose bus cable is browning out the servo under load.
hypotheses.check: Reseat the 3-pin cable at the elbow and check the 12 V supply holds under a move.

waiting.brief_subject: arm-1 down: clear elbow jam, spare servo ready
waiting.brief_body:
arm-1 (SO-101) is parked at home. Its elbow (elbow_flex) stalled at 2.9 N·m and stayed stuck in both directions, so the self-healer gave up.

1. Power off. Move the elbow by hand through its full range and clear whatever is jamming it.
2. Power on and jog the elbow ±20°. If it moves freely and stays under 60 °C, you're done.
3. If it still stalls, swap the elbow servo for the spare (Feetech STS3215 C018 12 V). Romulus has a cart ready for approval.

Reply to this email when the arm is back.
